summary: This synthetic evaluation approves the internal position. A short brief that tells each teammate what a section needs could help our contributions fit together, and the proposal explicitly lets us keep our shared document. I understand the value of trying the brief without treating that as a reason to buy or switch to a separate app. My main concern is that page placement is more prominent than the uneven depth that caused our group to revise together.
strengths: The position proposes section guidance rather than treating receipt of all contributions as proof that the writing is usable. That addresses a plausible improvement to the CR02 workflow.
The shared-document objection receives a credible answer: keep the document, test a short brief, and require a separate app to earn its place. This respects CR02's explicit doubt about switching.
Respect for existing writing and human discussion fits a group that already writes and revises together. The artifact does not require migration or payment to try the concept.
The document avoids measured time-saving claims and clearly distinguishes a proposed workflow from delivered features and synthetic tests from interview evidence.

nice_to_have.issue: The main language emphasizes deciding where material belongs more than making contributions comparable in depth.
nice_to_have.why_it_matters: CR02 already received everyone's contributions; the difficulty was combining very long sections with sections of only two sentences. As a synthetic judge, I would recognize my problem faster if the brief's intended benefit explicitly included clearer expectations about useful detail.
nice_to_have.suggested_change: Add a short sentence explaining that section prompts help contributors understand both what to include and the level of detail the group needs. Present this as a design intention to test, not a proven consistency outcome.

nice_to_have.issue: There is no concrete section-prompt example showing the proposed guidance.
nice_to_have.why_it_matters: CR02 expressed interest in knowing what each section should contain. An example would help me compare the proposed brief with instructions we could already put in our shared document. Its absence does not block approval of this internal position.
nice_to_have.suggested_change: Include one illustrative section purpose, two or three specific questions, and an example of useful detail that teammates could paste into the existing document. Label it as a proposed example rather than an interview-derived requirement.

open_questions: What would one section prompt actually ask each teammate, and how would it help us avoid very different levels of detail?
When we try the brief in our current document, does it reduce the reconciliation we need before putting the writing on the website?
If a separate app is later proposed, what additional benefit would justify its setup and possible cost over the shared-document brief?
evidence_limits: This is an AI synthetic artifact review based on the Casey persona and the supplied internal brand position; it is not a new interview or a verdict from the CR02 participant.

CR02 describes a four-person course project, not an established paid client or recurring professional workflow. Core audience fit here refers to the proposed activity of assembling other people's website contributions.
The group spent an evening revising and doing website work; the notes do not isolate content-editing time or support a quantified saving.

The score, verdict, suggested changes and anticipated benefits are synthetic judgments. The artifact describes a concept; no shipped feature, observed consistency improvement or reduction in revision work is established.
Approval of a reusable brief does not establish willingness to switch tools, pay or subscribe. CR02's budget, price ceiling and setup tolerance were not measured.
No Reddit research or other persona verdicts were used in this evaluation.
